assumptions: The numeric infusion-rate computation is represented as a simple stepwise adjustment: pressure above target lowers flow_rate by 1 and pressure below target raises it by 1, because the NL gives only the monotonic relationship and no exact control law.

AutocontrolInit automatically advances to AutocontrolNormal with a bare transition, because the NL names AutocontrolInit and normal autocontrol but does not specify an explicit initialization-complete event.
target_bp_command represents the caregiver-entered setpoint value used by the ChangeSetpoint event; the NL does not provide a concrete input variable name.
Manual is encoded as CA_mode = 0 and autocontrol as CA_mode = 1 because pyfcstm currently uses int variables for boolean-like or enumerated flags.

grounding_seeds.evidence_text: In the Mode_Control_Algorithm hierarchy, CARA has manual and autocontrol-related mode-control states plus an Ask_StartAC submode.
The pump has manual and autocontrol modes. In manual mode, pump speed is set with the built-in switch.
CARA has ... an Ask_StartAC submode; within Ask_StartAC, the setpoint can be changed and pressing StartAC enters AutocontrolInit.
During normal autocontrol, CARA controls flow rate only while there are no pump-operation complications.
If a pump fault such as fluid-tubing occlusion occurs, the pump activates alarm signals, the caregiver removes the fault, and when CARA was controlling the pump the software releases control.
The Caregiver Interface lets the caregiver ... initiate ... algorithmic pump control.
The Caregiver Interface lets the caregiver ... terminate algorithmic pump control.

decisions.rationale: Accepted because the hard-blocking scenario terminate_from_autocontrol_init_returns_manual hot-starts in CARA.Mode_Control_Algorithm.AutocontrolInit and injects CARA.Mode_Control_Algorithm.TerminateAC, expecting CARA.Mode_Control_Algorithm.Manual with CA_mode=0, software_control=0, pump_speed=manual_switch_speed/4, and flow_rate=default_flow_rate/3. scenario_results.name: default_init_enters_manual_and_uses_manual_settings

scenario_results.description: default-init: after dispatch to Manual, caregiver initiation enters Ask_StartAC, ChangeSetpoint updates target, StartAC enters AutocontrolInit, then initialization reaches AutocontrolNormal.
scenario_results.name: initiate_change_setpoint_start_autocontrol

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: TerminateAC during AutocontrolInit terminates algorithmic control and returns to Manual recovery operation.
scenario_results.name: terminate_from_autocontrol_init_returns_manual

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: in AutocontrolNormal with no pump fault, blood pressure above target lowers flow rate and drives control voltage/pump speed while logging.
scenario_results.name: autocontrol_high_pressure_lowers_flow

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: in AutocontrolNormal with no pump fault, blood pressure below target raises flow rate, and TerminateAC returns to Manual.
scenario_results.name: autocontrol_low_pressure_raises_flow_then_terminate

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: a pump fault during normal autocontrol enters PumpFault with alarm and software-control release, then FaultRemoved clears the fault and returns Manual.
scenario_results.name: pump_fault_enters_fault_state_and_fault_removed_recovers

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: CA_backManual from Ask_StartAC and CB_backManual from AutocontrolNormal both force the shared Manual recovery target.
scenario_results.name: fallback_ca_and_cb_force_manual_from_nonmanual_states

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start: CP_backManual from PumpFault and CC_backManual from AutocontrolInit both force CA_mode to Manual as the common recovery target.
scenario_results.name: fallback_cp_and_cc_force_manual_from_fault_and_init

evidence: DSL states include Manual, Ask_StartAC, AutocontrolInit, AutocontrolNormal, and PumpFault under Mode_Control_Algorithm.
Ask_StartAC -> Ask_StartAC on ChangeSetpoint updates target_bp; Ask_StartAC -> AutocontrolInit on StartAC.
AutocontrolNormal during lowers flow_rate when blood_pressure > target_bp and raises it when blood_pressure < target_bp.
Mode_Control_Algorithm during before stores shared_bp_buffer = blood_pressure.
PumpFault enter sets alarm_signal = 1 and software_control = 0.
Forced transitions ! * -> Manual exist for CA_backManual, CB_backManual, CP_backManual, and CC_backManual.
findings.summary: Core NL obligations are represented: manual/autocontrol states, Ask_StartAC setpoint/start behavior, monotonic blood-pressure-to-flow behavior, shared blood-pressure buffer, logging, fault alarm/release, and backManual recovery to Manual.

evidence: NL: CARA coordinates the Caregiver Interface, Blood Pressure Monitor, Algorithm, and Pump Monitors around an infusion pump.
Current DSL has a single root CARA with one Mode_Control_Algorithm hierarchy.
five_component_summary is empty.
Component roles are represented indirectly by variables/events such as blood_pressure, shared_bp_buffer, ChangeSetpoint, InitiateAC, TerminateAC, pump_fault, alarm_signal, and log_records.
findings.summary: The model covers the main behavioral roles but collapses the Caregiver Interface, Blood Pressure Monitor, Algorithm, and Pump/Pump Monitor responsibilities into one CARA hierarchy with shared variables rather than distinct component structure.

evidence: NL: Caregiver Interface displays and sounds error messages.
DSL uses only alarm_signal and has no separate display_message or audible_alarm representation.
NL: Algorithm records infusion-related data in log files.
DSL abstracts this as log_records = log_records + 1 in AutocontrolNormal.
findings.summary: Some secondary NL outputs are only abstractly represented or not separately represented, especially display/sound error messages and log-file records.

evidence: DSL: if blood_pressure > target_bp then flow_rate = flow_rate - 1; else if blood_pressure < target_bp then flow_rate = flow_rate + 1.
GroundingMap assumption: numeric infusion-rate computation is represented as a simple stepwise adjustment because the NL gives only the monotonic relationship and no exact control law.
findings.summary: The infusion-rate algorithm is reduced to a one-unit step adjustment. This is grounded as a monotonic abstraction, but it is not a detailed control law.

evidence: DSL has forced transitions ! * -> Manual for CA_backManual, CB_backManual, CP_backManual, and CC_backManual.
DSL PumpFault -> Manual on FaultRemoved clears pump_fault and alarm_signal.
Forced transitions to Manual do not explicitly clear pump_fault or alarm_signal.
Simulation sample fallback_cp_and_cc_force_manual_from_fault_and_init shows CP_backManual from PumpFault reaches Manual while alarm_signal remains 1.
findings.summary: Recovery behavior is broadly NL-grounded, but forced backManual transitions can move to Manual from PumpFault without using FaultRemoved; this may permit Manual state while a fault/alarm condition remains active. This is advisory because the NL explicitly says backManual events make Manual the shared recovery target.

evidence: design_diagnostics_summary reports blocking_count = 0 and advisory_count = 19.
W_HIGH_VAR_TO_LEAF_RATIO: variable-to-leaf ratio 2.8 exceeds threshold 2.0.
Multiple W_UNREFERENCED_VAR diagnostics are reported for CA_mode, blood_pressure, shared_bp_buffer, target_bp, flow_rate, pump_speed, control_voltage, alarm_signal, software_control, and log_records.
These variables correspond to NL obligations such as shared buffer, pump speed, alarm signal, software control, target blood pressure, and logging.
findings.summary: The model has advisory structural smells from many output/state variables that do not participate in guards and a high variable-to-leaf ratio, but these variables are mostly NL-grounded outputs or environmental inputs.

findings.summary: No evidence of an unjustified local warning fix is present. The current candidate appears to retain NL-grounded variables rather than deleting them merely to satisfy advisory diagnostics.
